says: In today's tooling, Quotes ends a patch's hunk only at a diff line, so in a file under patches/ written as a plain unified diff (no diff line between files) the second file's +++ header is read as inside a hunk and now skips the em dash, where main's script caught it; the --- header had the same gap before this change. Every file in patches/ today has diff --git lines, so nothing hits it now.
proof: A draft patches/u@1.patch holding '--- a/x.js', '+++ b/x.js', '@@ -1 +1 @@', '-a', '+b', '--- a/y.js', '+++ b/y.js <em dash>', '@@ -1 +1 @@', '-c', '+d': leakgrep.sh --text at 19e9165ff printed 'added text clean' and exited 0; main's leakgrep.sh printed 'leak em_dash at added line 7' and exited 1.
cost: An em dash on a header line of a non-git-format file under patches/ passes the style check; no secret, path, name or private-word shape is affected.
